summary: Materials (XMJ +4.06%) drove the ASX 200's sharpest single-session gain in months (+1.98% to 8,804.0), erasing Thursday's four-month-low close, after Trump's overnight decision to call off planned Iran strikes triggered a broad Wall Street risk-on bounce (SPX +1.75%, VIX -12.5%) and collapsed oil (WTI -4.68%, Brent -6.1%). The de-escalation/commodity-ETF surge flowed directly into ASX resources, with lithium (LTR +9.82%, PLS +9.76%, ELV +12.49%, DVP +10.37%, MI6 +14.67%) and gold miners (GMD +10.83%, PNR +9.57%, BC8 +9.77%) leading 10 of 11 sectors higher. Breadth was exceptionally wide (XJO adv/dec 4.4:1, XTO 4.7:1), with XJO and XTO back above both 50MA and 200MA for the first time in over a week despite lagging 'Neutral Bear' regime labels. Energy (XEJ -0.46%) was the lone notable laggard, mirroring the overnight oil collapse, with VEA -3.43% the standout. The RBA's Tuesday 16 June decision looms as the next key catalyst - a hold at 4.35% is near-certain (42/45 economists), but messaging tone is flagged as the real risk given 10 of 11 developed-market central banks are now priced for further tightening.
